title: Cut Off Trees for Golf Event
summary: Given an m x n matrix representing a forest, where 0 indicates an impassable cell, 1 represents an empty cell, and numbers greater than 1 represent trees of varying heights, you need to cut off all the trees in ascending order of their height starting from the cell (0, 0).
statement: Given an m x n matrix representing a forest, where 0 indicates an impassable cell, 1 represents an empty cell, and numbers greater than 1 represent trees of varying heights, you need to cut off all the trees in ascending order of their height starting from the cell (0, 0). Each step can be in one of the four directions: north, east, south, or west. If you cannot cut off all the trees, return -1.
constraints: 0 is blocked, 1 is walkable, and each value above 1 is a uniquely tall tree.
Starting at (0,0), visit and cut every tree in increasing height order using four-directional steps.
hints: Tree heights fix the visit order, leaving only shortest paths between consecutive targets.
Sort tree cells and run BFS from the current position to each next tree.
Accumulate each BFS distance; return -1 on an unreachable target.
Any valid cutting walk must visit the same target sequence, and replacing each segment by its shortest route is independently optimal.
editorial: Any valid cutting walk must visit the same target sequence, and replacing each segment by its shortest route is independently optimal.

tests.explanation: The increasing-height route follows the accessible perimeter in six steps.
The blocked middle row makes the lower trees unreachable.
